pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql; test 'AC-1' checks all three rows are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
test 'AC-2' asserts ★ on the starred item and none on the others.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 then 1 and expects id order ★ First, ★ Third.
test 'AC-4' checks / and ?show=all in id order.

The code implements both links, but the last commit 390d2f7 renamed the test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. No test names AC-5 and the spec doesn't mark it verified by review, so it counts as unmet.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.

findings.what: The follow-up commit 390d2f7 ('Follow-up edits') removed the 'AC-5:' prefix from the link test's title. No test names AC-5 now, which makes it unmet under the spec rules. The commit reads like a quiet way to drop the traceability.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'.

findings.what: The AC-7 test only checks that routes.json contains the string. It does not check that the traffic worker requests the path with its query intact.
findings.fix: Optionally add a traffic test that the worker calls the app with /?show=starred.

lenses.note: A spec exists; the code follows both decisions (id order kept, query parameter, GET only).
AC-5 has no test naming it after commit 390d2f7. All four state-table rows have tests that check the list, message and link.

The tests assert behaviour. The test runner could not be run here (the cloudflare:workers pool); CI is assumed to run it. The traffic fake-app change adds the query string to the recorded path and loosens nothing.
The README mentions ?show=starred. It doesn't mention the 'Starred only' and 'All items' links, but that is minor.
The view is validated with Object.hasOwn, and the SQL is built only from fixed view constants. No defects found.
Titles are escaped, the query is not interpolated, and no planted instructions were found. The route regex relaxation is limited to allowing '?'.
The diff touches no CSS, template or UI asset files; the HTML is plain and unstyled.
No browser flow is available or claimed; the PR states no screenshots.

The PR claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the last commit renamed the AC-5 test and dropped its AC id. The PR also says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is consistent. The title is under 72 characters.
